correctness.rationale: Projection reduction from Algorithm 1 and the prior-direction H-orthogonality is proved directly. An absolutely continuous Gaussian direction in a hyperplane of dimension d−1 hits a fixed nonzero error vector with probability zero when d≥3, and necessarily aligns when d=2. Orthogonal projections onto random isotropic lines leave beta-distributed norm factors; their past-independent conditional laws prove independence. Beta means and integrable log factors prove the exact mean and almost-sure exponent. Exact Fraction recurrence checks, 450 two-dimensional runs, and 40,000 isotropic random paths corroborate finite cases without being substituted for proof.
